cases.caption: Historical checkpoint comparison for dem01-hertz-tsuji. Panels (a) and (b) show position (x component) and velocity (x component) of the selected body 'left'; (c) shows the signed FunDEM-minus-reference residual of (a). Black open diamonds denote pinned LAMMPS saved-state references; blue open circles, orange crosses, green open squares and purple plus signs denote CPU at Δt, GPU at Δt, CPU at Δt/2 and GPU at Δt/2, respectively. Every run uses its retained physical checkpoint times; no time shift, jitter, averaging, fitting or connecting trajectory is used. Coincident symbols are retained with different shapes and sizes. Axes state physical units and explicit powers of ten. Panel (d) shows recomputed error divided by its stated tolerance; the dashed vertical line is the acceptance boundary ε/τ = 1. Absolute errors are |actual−expected|; relative errors divide this by |expected|. Total x momentum: absolute tolerance 1.41371669412e-05; Restitution: relative tolerance 0.02. Exactly 4 zero ratios are displayed at the explicit logarithmic floor 0.00245383944556; every positive ratio is unmodified. The four run markers have deterministic vertical offsets within each categorical criterion row solely to distinguish coincident values. These sparse historical checkpoints do not establish a new validation outcome for the current source or a continuous-time error bound.

panels.zeroConvention: Only exact-zero ratios are placed at the stated positive display floor; all positive ratios retain their true values.

cases.caption: Retained Hertz-contact measurements for dem02-hertz-twosphere. Panels (a) and (b) show contact overlap and normal-force magnitude at the three retained physical checkpoint times for each run. Their black dashed lines denote the continuum analytical maxima $\delta_{\mathrm{max}}$ and $F_{\mathrm{max}}$, not LAMMPS saved-state trajectories. Panel (c) shows signed total-energy drift $(E_{\mathrm{tot}}-E_0)/E_0$, where $E_{\mathrm{tot}}=K+U_H$ and the dashed zero line denotes conservation of the retained initial energy $E_0$. Here $E_0=1.17286125734\,\mathrm{J}$. Blue open circles, orange crosses, green open squares and purple plus signs denote CPU at $\Delta t$, GPU at $\Delta t$, CPU at $\Delta t/2$ and GPU at $\Delta t/2$, respectively. All numerical checkpoint observations remain unconnected symbols at their original times; overlapping runs are neither averaged nor shifted. Pair-level contact and total-energy columns are duplicated for the left and right spheres in the retained table; one identical copy is plotted, without summing the pair twice. Panel (d) shows error divided by its stated limit. The $U_H(t_c)$ row is the official sampled criterion $U_H(t_c)=(2/5)F_n(t_c)\delta(t_c)$ against $E_0$, at $t_c=30.16\,\mu\mathrm{s}$. The $\delta_{\mathrm{max}}$ and $F_{\mathrm{max}}$ rows are separately declared global-peak diagnostics; the final row is the retained whole-event maximum $|\Delta E/E_0|$. Each uses a 0.01 limit; only the first row is the named official energy assertion. Global scalar summaries are read from HISTORICAL-RESULTS.csv, not inferred from the three checkpoints or assigned guessed peak times. The dashed vertical acceptance boundary is error/limit = 1. Exactly 0 zero ratios are displayed at the explicit logarithmic floor 6.96502326976e-07; positive ratios are unchanged. Run markers have fixed vertical offsets within each categorical diagnostic row. These historical measurements preserve the recorded outcome and do not constitute a new simulation or continuous-time validation.
cases.selectedBody: left/right contact pair (one duplicated scalar copy)
